label: Pleomorphic_Adenoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts

- Most common benign salivary gland tumor; peak incidence in parotid, also frequent in minor salivary glands
- Hallmark: biphasic epithelial and myoepithelial components in chondromyxoid stroma
- PLAG1 and HMGA2 gene rearrangements are characteristic molecular alterations
- Recurrence risk increases with incomplete excision due to pseudopod extensions and satellite nodules
- Malignant transformation possible (carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma), though uncommon
- Capsule is typically complete in major glands (parotid), incomplete or absent in minor glands

## Terminology

- Definition: Benign salivary gland neoplasm composed of a mix of ductal (epithelial), myoepithelial, and variable stromal elements (classically chondromyxoid)
- Synonyms: Benign mixed tumor (historical); PA (abbreviation)
- Not recommended: "Congenital pleomorphic adenoma" (obsolete for "salivary gland anlage tumor") [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Salivary_Gland_Anlage_Tumour.html)

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria

- **Essential:**
  - Biphasic architecture: both epithelial (ductal/glandular) and myoepithelial (spindle, plasmacytoid, clear) cell components [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
  - Prominent chondromyxoid or myxoid, and/or hyalinized stroma [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
  - Well-circumscribed and encapsulated in major glands (parotid and submandibular); circumscribed but often unencapsulated in minor glands (palate, oral cavity)
  - No evidence of infiltrative growth (except for characteristic pseudopodic extensions which remain benign) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
- **Desirable:**
  - Cytologic blandness, low mitotic activity
  - PLAG1 or HMGA2 gene rearrangements (~70% of cases; highly supportive)
  - Varied stromal elements: chondroid, myxoid, hyalinized, occasionally osseous [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
  - Capsule breaches with pseudopods on histology (increasing recurrence risk if incompletely excised)
  - Cytologic and IHC: positivity for both epithelial and myoepithelial markers

## Etiology/Pathogenesis

- Molecular:
  - PLAG1 gene rearrangement characteristic (~70%)
  - HMGA2 rearrangements less frequent, but supportive
- Notable for biphasic ductal/myoepithelial proliferation; myoepithelial variation accounts for stromal diversity (chondroid/myxoid/hyalinized) [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)

## Clinical Issues

- Epidemiology:
  - Most common benign salivary gland tumor [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
  - Broad age range, average middle-aged adults, slight female predominance
- Site:
  - Parotid gland (majority)
  - Minor salivary glands (hard palate most common, followed by upper lip and buccal mucosa)
- Presentation:
  - Painless, slow-growing, mobile mass; may be fixed in hard palate lesions
- Natural History:
  - Recurrence risk higher if incomplete excision or tumor spillage
    - Recurrent tumors may present as multiple nodules ("satellite nodules")
- Treatment:
  - Surgical excision with margin of normal tissue, especially in parotid to avoid recurrence
- Prognosis:
  - Excellent when completely excised
  - Malignant transformation to carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma reported, especially in long-standing or recurrent tumors

## Macroscopic

- Well-circumscribed, round to oval mass; typically encapsulated in major glands
- Firm, whitish-tan cut surface, variably bosselated or lobulated
- Parotid lesions: completely encapsulated [Fig. 20-4, Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p0978_fig01_fig_20_4.jpeg)
- Minor gland (palate): circumscribed, often not encapsulated [Hn Atlas](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p0979_fig01_fig_20_6.jpeg)
- Recurrent tumors: multinodular, multiple satellite nodules within the surgical bed [Hn Gnepp](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/_asset_library/textbooks/Hn_Gnepp/page_images/Hn_Gnepp_page_0472.png)
- May demonstrate “pseudopods” or small extensions into surrounding fat

![Encapsulated, well-circumscribed, sometimes multinodular gross appearance of pleomorphic adenoma.](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_gnepp/hn_gnepp_p0472_fig01_fig_6_12.jpeg)

## Microscopic

- Biphasic epithelial (ductal/glandular) and myoepithelial components
  - Myoepithelial cells often spindle, plasmacytoid, or even clear cell morphology
  - Duct-like and tubular/glandular structures, often double-layered
- Chondromyxoid and/or myxoid to hyalinized stroma [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
- Stromal elements may predominate, with areas that mimic cartilage
- Well-circumscribed and usually encapsulated (major gland); minor gland lesions lack true capsule but remain sharply circumscribed
- Pseudopodic extensions—narrow tongues of tumor protruding through the capsule—may be present
- Commixed morphology: solid, trabecular, cystic, and even papillary patterns may occur
- Rare squamous or oncocytic metaplasia
- Absence of cytologic atypia or high mitotic activity
- Recurrent tumors: multinodular with similar biphasic/stromal features
- Capsular invasion or extension into fat alone does not indicate carcinoma

![Triphasic nature—epithelial, myoepithelial, and stromal components—in pleomorphic adenoma.](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-public-figures-830130787988/textbook_figures_web_v1/hn_atlas/hn_atlas_p0979_fig01_fig_20_6.jpeg)

## Ancillary Tests

- Immunohistochemistry:
  - Epithelial cells: cytokeratin+, EMA+
  - Myoepithelial cells: S100+, SOX10+, GFAP+, p63+, calponin+, SMA+
  - Nuclear PLAG1 IHC (where available) supportive
- Molecular:
  - PLAG1 gene rearrangement, often detectable by FISH in ~70% [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html)
  - HMGA2 rearrangements in a minority of cases
- Cytology:
  - Fine-needle aspiration: biphasic smear with bland, cohesive epithelial cells; background of fibrillary, magenta (mucoid/myxoid) matrix; spindle myoepithelial cells

## Differential Diagnosis

- **Basal cell adenoma** ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Basal_Cell_Adenoma.html))
  - More monomorphic, lacks chondromyxoid stroma
  - Biphasic basaloid morphology with peripheral palisading
  - Dual cell population shown by IHC; nuclear β-catenin reactivity
- **Myoepithelioma** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html))
  - Lacks significant ductal/epithelial (glandular/tubular) component
  - Nearly pure myoepithelial proliferation, often sclerotic or myxoid background
  - May overlap in IHC, but absence of true glandular elements defines
- **Adenomatoid hyperplasia / Sialadenosis** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenomatoidhyperplasia.html))
  - Non-neoplastic; coalescing lobules of normal acini
  - Lacks encapsulation, chondromyxoid stroma, and biphasic neoplastic features
- **Canalicular adenoma** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandscanalicularadenoma.html))
  - Almost exclusively upper lip; cords/strands of columnar epithelial cells
  - Lacks myxoid/chondroid stroma and biphasic histology
- **Oncocytoma** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsoncocytosis.html))
  - Sheets of oncocytic cells; lacks biphasic pattern and chondromyxoid stroma
- **Sclerosing polycystic adenoma** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandssclerosingpolycysticadenoma.html))
  - Cystic/diffuse sclerosing stroma, not biphasic
- **Adenoid cystic carcinoma** ([Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html))
  - Infiltrative, usually cribriform (“Swiss cheese”) or tubular architecture
  - Greater cytologic atypia and perineural invasion
- **Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma**
  - Areas of overt malignancy arising in, or adjacent to, classic pleomorphic adenoma features
  - Invasive carcinoma component (e.g., salivary duct, adenocarcinoma NOS) with cytologic atypia, mitoses, possible necrosis

Caveats:
- Presence of pseudopodic outgrowths into capsule or adjacent fat does not itself define malignancy in pleomorphic adenoma, but may increase recurrence risk if excised incompletely [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandspleomorphicadenoma.html).

cards.title: Salivary gland myoepithelioma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Salivary gland myoepithelioma Section: differential_diagnosis The well-defined borders of the tumour and the lack of invasive growth distinguish ME from myoepithelial carcinoma. The characteristic basaloid biphasic pattern, peripheral palisading, and minimal to absent myxoid stroma of basal cell adenoma help to separate it from ME. Monomorphic histology and rare or absent ductal structures in ME separate it from pleomorphic adenoma. Distinguishing from soft tissue ME may be difficult, given the overlapping histological features and the presence of PLAG1 gene rearrangements in both.

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Benign tumor: surgical resection with negative margin is considered curative
cards.excerpt:
Enucleation is associated with 15 - 25% risk of local recurrence
Recurrences are usually within 18 months but can be up to 50 years later (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2008;132:1445)
Risk of malignant transformation is ~5%
Risk factors for malignant transformation: multiple recurrences, submandibular location, older age, larger size, prominent hyalinization, increased mitotic rate (if present, sample tumor more thoroughly), radiation exposure

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typically has 3 components
cards.excerpt:
Epithelial (ductal) component forming the inner layer of cysts and tubules
Myoepithelial cells as the outer layer of cysts and tubules and scattered within the myxoid stroma
Cytology of myoepithelial cells can be plasmacytoid, spindled, epithelioid, clear or stellate shaped

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Stromal component is typically myxoid, chondroid or myxochondroid
cards.excerpt:
It can also be hyalinized or fibrotic
Metaplastic changes may be seen, e.g. adipose metaplasia, osseous metaplasia, squamous metaplasia (sometimes with keratinization), sebaceous metaplasia and mucinous metaplasia
Intravascular permeation has been reported in a small percentage of cases and does not increase the risk of recurrence or distant metastasis
It is proposed to be a phenomenon associated with surgical manipulation (Am J Surg Pathol 2012;36:1674)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Typical feature is its unique fibrillary stroma
cards.excerpt:
Mixture of myoepithelial cells, ductal cells and extracellular stroma
Myoepithelial cells are usually the predominant cell type with various cytomorphology, including round, polygonal, plasmacytoid, spindle, etc.
Ductal cells show bland cytologic features with organized honeycombing or ductal arrangement
Extracellular matrix shows characteristic feathery / fibrillary borders and bright magenta color on Romanowsky type stain and gray-green chondromyxoid features on Papanicolaou stain
Cytology imagesContributed by Bin Xu, M.D., Ph.D., Jen-Fan Hang, M.D. and Shuanzeng (Sam) Wei, M.D., Ph.D.

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Goblet cell
cards.excerpt:
Positive stains
Ductal (epithelial) cells are typically positive for cytokeratins (e.g. AE1 / AE3, CAM5.2 and CK7)
Myoepithelial cells are positive for GFAP, S100, SOX10, actin - alpha smooth muscle, calponin, p40 and p63
PLAG1 and HMGA2 can be used as surrogate immunohistochemical markers for underlying PLAG1 or HMGA2 fusion (Histopathology 2018;72:285, Histopathology 2017;71:511)

cards.title: Pleomorphic adenoma — Circumscribed tumor Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.heading: Circumscribed tumor Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.text_excerpt:
Admixture of epithelial and myoepithelial cells embedded in a chondromyxoid stroma, may show chondroid or osseous metaplasia
Architecture includes tubules, islands, cords, trabeculae, sheets or pseudoglandular structures lined by 2 cell types
Inner epithelial cells: cuboidal or columnar epithelial cells, with or without apocrine or squamous metaplasia
Outer myoepithelial cells: polygonal, plasmacytoid, fusiform or stellate with clear to eosinophilic cytoplasm
